english.title: Attempt common assault of an emergency worker
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) attempted to assault **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..), an emergency worker, namely **(..SPECIFY TYPE OF EMERGENCY WORKER..), acting in the exercise of

(A)_[his]_
(B)_[her]_

functions as such a worker
english.legislation: Contrary to section 39 of the Criminal Justice Act 1988 and section 1 of the Assaults on Emergency Workers (Offences) Act 2018 and section 1(1) of the Criminal Attempts Act 1981.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
attempted to
unlawfully assault
an emergency worker
who was acting in the exercise of his / her functions as such a worker

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) On the 28th June 2022, the penalty for offences under this section was increased on indictment from a maximum of 12 months imprisonment to 2 years imprisonment by section 2 of the Police, Crime, Sentencing and Courts Act 2022. For the offence applying from the 28th June 2022, see H100763.
(ii) This is an aggravated version of the offence in document H7993; committing assault against an emergency worker acting in the exercise of his / her functions as such as worker, carries a higher penalty, as per section 1 of the Assaults on emergency Workers (Offences) Act 2018.

other.penalty:
Either way -

Summary: maximum 12 months imprisonment and/or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 12 months imprisonment and/or a fine.

Note:
For offences committed before 2nd May 2022 the maximum penalty on summary conviction is six months.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
